title: MACD in plain words
desc: Two averages, their gap and the bars, and why crosses come late

cards.title: The crossover
cards.situation: The MACD line just crossed above its signal line. The stock is already up 5% from its low. What does the cross tell you?

chart.label: Price bottoms at $50; the MACD line crosses above its signal later, at $52.50

options.text: The bottom is happening right now
options.feedback: MACD is built from moving averages, so it lags. The cross confirms a turn that started earlier.

options.text: Momentum turned up: it confirms a move already under way
options.feedback: The cross says momentum has turned. It comes after the low, never at it.
The cross says nothing about how far price goes. It only confirms that momentum turned up after the low.

cards.work: Low $50. The cross came at $52.50: price was already up 5%.

cards.title: Two averages and their gap
cards.text: [[macd|MACD]] takes a **fast** exponential average of price (12 days) and a **slow** one (26 days). Exponential means recent days count more. The gap between them is the MACD line.

blocks.tip: Gap growing: momentum building. Gap shrinking: momentum fading. Above zero: the fast average is above the slow one.

cards.title: Read the bars
cards.text: The bars show the gap between the MACD line and its signal line. Watch them grow, then shrink.

chart.label: The MACD bars grow, peak and shrink while price keeps climbing

cards.foot: Price kept climbing after the bars peaked. Shrinking bars mean the push is fading, not that price must fall.

cards.title: Crosses in a choppy market
cards.text: When price goes sideways, the two lines cross back and forth. Each cross looks like a signal. Most go nowhere.

chart.label: Sideways price; the MACD lines cross back and forth five times

cards.rule: a cross confirms a trend. It’s never a reason on its own.

cards.title: Above zero
cards.q: The MACD line is above zero. What does that mean?

options.text: The fast average is above the slow one
options.feedback: Above zero means the fast average sits above the slow one: recent prices average higher than older ones.
MACD is built from price only. It knows nothing about the company’s profits.
MACD only describes the past. Above zero means recent prices average higher than older ones.
MACD doesn’t use volume. Above zero means the fast average is above the slow one.

cards.title: Always after
cards.q: Why do MACD crossovers usually come after a turn has already started?

options.text: They’re built from moving averages, which lag
options.feedback: Averages of past prices turn after price does, so a MACD cross confirms a turn rather than calls it.

options.text: The data arrives a day late
options.feedback: The data isn’t late. The lag comes from averaging past prices: the averages turn after price does.

options.text: They use volume, which comes later
options.feedback: MACD doesn’t use volume at all. It lags because it’s built from moving averages of past prices.
MACD can’t see ahead. It’s made of averages of past prices, so its crosses come after the turn.

cards.headline: You can read MACD in plain words.
lines: MACD is the gap between a fast and a slow average.
The signal line and bars show momentum building or fading.
Crossovers lag, and whipsaw when the market goes sideways.
